brewing.notes: A safe starting point for green tea: cooler water, short steeps, then adjust by taste.

description:
A flat single-bud green tea from the Jinfeng Mountains in Naxi, Luzhou, Sichuan, named for its likeness to a sparrow's tongue.

Treat it as you would any green tea: cooler water, short steeps, and a seller who can say where and when it was picked.
history: Legend says a monk of a temple below the mountain named it in the late Ming or early Qing. In 2006 it received a tourism-goods honour at a travel fair in Chengdu. Little more is documented.
processing: Typical of green tea: picked, heated soon after picking to stop oxidation, then shaped and dried.
harvest_season: Tender single buds, early February to early March.
appearance_dry: Flat and straight, a vivid jade green.
taste_profile: Rich, lasting chestnut aroma; fresh, mellow and clean.
vintage_note: Green teas like this are normally sold as the current year's harvest and are best within a year of picking. It is not an ageing tea.
